complexity.notes: The pop-and-expand approach is correct and achieves amortized O(n) since each element is removed from the set at most once. The worst case degrades to O(n^2) under adversarial hash collisions in the set membership checks. A common alternative idiom only expands from sequence starts (checking num-1 not in set first), which avoids some redundant membership tests but has the same asymptotic complexity.
complexity.summary: Builds a set of the numbers, then repeatedly pops an arbitrary element and expands outward in both directions, removing each consecutive element from the set so every value is processed exactly once. Tracks the maximum run length found.
